es.hot_ram_to_data.quote: The typical memory:data ratio for the hot zone used is 1:30 and for the warm zone is 1:160

es.warm_ram_to_data.quote: ... and for the warm zone is 1:160

es.frozen_ram_to_data.quote: a frozen tier node will jump up to 100 TB ... This amounts to a 1:1500 RAM-to-storage ratio

es.frozen_cache_fraction.quote: With a typical 10% local cache size

es.low_watermark.quote: cluster.routing.allocation.disk.watermark.low ... Defaults to 85%, meaning that Elasticsearch will not allocate shards to nodes that have more than 85% disk used

es.replicas_across_azs.quote: With allocation awareness on the zone attribute (a multi-AZ setup), Elasticsearch places copies 'ensuring (if possible) that no two copies of the same shard are in the same rack', so each replicated byte crosses an AZ boundary; AWS bills $0.01/GB in each direction (prices.json, 'Data transfer EC2 <-> EC2 across AZs, same region'). Bytes counted = raw ingest, (the JSON documents shipped are larger)

cartridge.node_disk_max_gb.quote: A gp3 volume can range in size from 1 GiB to 64 TiB (one gp3 volume per node; GiB taken as GB, conservative)

elastic.subscription.enterprise_features.unit: flag (1 = an Enterprise subscription is needed for these features)
elastic.subscription.enterprise_features.quote: Subscription matrix, Data management: 'Searchable snapshots' is ticked only in the Enterprise column; 'Data tiers' and 'Index lifecycle management' are ticked under 'Free and open - Basic'. Footnote 15: 'Synthetic _source is an Enterprise feature from 8.17 onward.' The frozen tier is searchable snapshots (partially mounted), so it needs Enterprise; hot/warm with ILM does not.

es.warm_instance_profile.unit: disk GB per GB RAM on Elastic's warm profile (i3en)
es.warm_instance_profile.quote: Elastic's AWS hardware table lists the dense-storage warm/frozen profile aws.data.highstorage.i3en at disk:memory 74:1. Self-managed warm nodes here use EC2 i3en.3xlarge (7500 GB NVMe / 96 GiB = 78:1), the same family.
